title: fix(spec)!: `CronSchedule.timezone` is judged by the `iana_time_zone` membership predicate
body:
Fixes #16292

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

`CronScheduleSchema.timezone` was a bare `z.string().optional().default('UTC')`, so `defineJob` and `JobSchema.parse` took `timezone: 'UTC+8'` at authoring and build time and said nothing. The value then reached `CronJobAdapter.schedule`, croner threw, and `AppPlugin` logged a per-job `FAILED TO SCHEDULE` at `error` level: the job was declared and never ran, and its author learned that from a boot log in whatever environment started first.

It is now judged by `isValueDomainMember('iana_time_zone', ...)` — the predicate `@objectstack/spec/shared` already exports, in the same package as the schema, and the same judge the four `valueDomain: 'iana_time_zone'` columns (`sys_business_unit.timezone`, `sys_organization.timezone`, `sys_job.timezone`, `sys_report_schedule.timezone`) are written against. `sys_job.timezone` is a write-only mirror, so that column never judges the value the scheduler honours; this is the separate, earlier door.

## What was measured before any code was written

The dispatch carried three mechanism assumptions. All three were re-measured on `origin/main` at `eeaa882459` and all three hold.

1. **The schema is still unvalidated.** `packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts` carried `timezone: z.string().optional().default('UTC')` verbatim. The card's premise is alive.
2. **The predicate is an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` probe**, so the accept set is the host's tz database, not a checked-in list. Measured on this container's Node, which is the repo's pinned baseline (`.nvmrc` = `22`, every workflow pins `node-version: '22'`):

   ```
   node v22.22.2 · icu 78.2 · unicode 17.0 · tz 2025c · full-icu (de-DE month renders "Januar")
   Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone').length = 418
   MEMBER  UTC · Asia/Kolkata · America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires · Europe/Kyiv
   MEMBER  Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh · US/Eastern · GMT · Pacific/Chatham · Africa/Juba · europe/zurich
   REFUSED UTC+8 · GMT+8 · Mars/Olympus · Europe/Munich · China Standard Time · ""
   ```

   The triage seat's fence was: measure this first, and if the build environment's ICU is not full, stop and report instead of narrowing. It is full, and `Asia/Kolkata` and `America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires` — the two zones that comment named — are both members. The exposure this adds is also not a new class: the same probe already decides those four columns, the settings door and `resolveAuthzContext`, so parse time and schedule time give one answer on one host.
3. **The four-column precedent exists**, and the spelling followed here is the repo's own (`isValueDomainMember`), not a new one.

## The test, and why it pins no zone list

A test enumerating zones would be a verdict about this container's tz database rather than about the schema. The invariant that belongs to this schema is that its verdict **equals** `isValueDomainMember('iana_time_zone', ...)` for every input, on whatever host runs it — so that is what the corpus test asserts. Only two ends are asserted absolutely, and both are ICU-independent: `'UTC'` (the key's own declared default, which ECMA-402 requires of every runtime, so an omitted key can never be refused) and `'UTC+8'` (an offset that names no zone). The zone-by-zone traps stay pinned once, where the predicate lives, in `packages/spec/src/shared/value-domain.test.ts`.

## Reverse verification

Direction predicted before the run: **goes red**. Run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, from the committed state, so the mutation and its restore are proved against the disk rather than against an exit code. The test resolves `./job.zod` relatively, in-package, so this ablation has no `dist/` leg.

```
ablation-replace: anchor "timezone: CronTimezoneSchema.optional().default('UTC')" x1 (before)
ablation-replace: anchor   x1 -> x0
ablation-replace: blob     e485798a9f19df3305d9b080f3a92f32bc2e560d -> 96bc817c4b05eda7888ee0fdf65928f7f33a15f4
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob e485798a9f19 -> 96bc817c4b05
  Tests  3 failed | 52 passed (55)
    x agrees with the shared predicate on every input
    x refuses `UTC+8` with a located issue instead of carrying it to the scheduler
    x refuses through `defineJob`, located at `schedule.timezone`
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (e485798a9f19) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Restored leg: 55 passed (55). The two new tests that survive the ablation are the two written to survive it — the default still parsing, and the zoneless `interval` / `once` branches being untouched.

## The changeset level, answered from the repo's rules

The dispatch asked this as an open question and told me to answer it from the repo or return `needs_decision`. The repo decides it, in two places that agree:

- `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, in its own header: during the launch window `major` is refused and *"breaking changes ship as `minor`"*; its stated END CONDITION is that at GA *"a required member on a published interface, an **accept-set narrowing**, or any compile-breaking change to implementers grades `major`"* — so until GA the narrowing collapses onto `minor`, the highest level available. The same header, and the `Check Changeset` prose in `pr-automation.yml`, both state that during the window the level is **not** the breaking-ness carrier: *"the mandatory information carriers for breaking-ness in the meantime are the BREAKING banner the author writes in the changeset body and the ADR-0087 migration-ledger disposition"*.
- Landed changesets for the same act say the same thing in words. `.changeset/17499-groupbyfield-non-padded.md` is the closest analogue in the tree — three published authoring keys that were bare `z.string()` gain a refinement — and it reads *"Shipped as `minor` under the repo's launch-window convention for accept-set narrowings"*. `.changeset/18835-list-view-unwalked-field-naming-keys.md` repeats the sentence.

So: `minor`, plus a `**BREAKING**` banner, plus an ADR-0087 disposition. The disposition taken is `not-required`, category `no-migration-prescription` — the same category `.changeset/18124-genuine-duration-rows-declare-their-unit.md` took for the same shape. No key, export, config field or stored shape is added, removed, renamed or re-spelled; the refusal is value-level and undecidable in the upgrade direction, because an offset spelling such as `UTC+8` names no zone and nothing can derive which real zone its author meant. `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing mechanical to apply. `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` reads the changeset as `[BREAKING+bang+clause-2-narrowing]` and accepts that disposition; exit 0.

Not `already-registered` against `platform-timezone-columns-iana-domain-refused` (the sibling narrowing from #16421): that entry covers the two columns, and the gate's own header says it verifies only that an id resolves and pre-dates the base, never that it covers the change. This is a different door and is deliberately not filed under it.

## No new error code, and what that does to clause 2

The dispatch asked for this explicitly, either way. **No `StandardErrorCode` member is registered and none is needed.** A Zod refinement answers with an `issue.code` of `custom` located on the key; the ADR-0114 field code `value_domain` belongs to ObjectQL's record write path, which this change does not touch. Measured on the diff: no schema key, no closed-set member, no published export and no registry row is added — `check:api-surface`, `check:api-surface-declarations`, `check:export-origins` and `check:declaration-map` are all green with no regeneration, and `CronTimezoneSchema` is a module-local const.

⚠️ So the honest arm by the charter's own reading (「收窄仍是契约面,不触条款②」) is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The line above reads `yes` because the claim comment on the card declares `yes`, and the claim itself records why: the seat could not rule out a new error code or export, and over-declaring is never the auditable error. That question is now measured, and it came back negative — a reviewing seat can overturn the `yes` on this evidence. The arm `(narrowing)` is the honest direction either way, and it is the token the breaking-ness detector reads.

## Scope

Declared file surface was `packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/value-domain.zod.ts` and their sibling tests. `value-domain.zod.ts` needed no edit — the predicate it exports was already the right one — so it is untouched. Two paths outside that surface are in the diff, both mandatory consequences rather than scope growth, and both declared here:

- `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` — `z.toJSONSchema()` has no arm for a `custom` check, so the new rule reaches the runtime and not `packages/spec/json-schema/**`. The build refuses until the gap is a reviewed line, and it printed the seven sites (three new published schemas, four `api/*` envelopes that embed a job manifest). The ledger is hand-edited by design and has no generator.
- `content/docs/references/system/job.mdx` — auto-generated, regenerated by `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:docs` because the key's `.describe()` now states the rule it enforces.

`packages/spec/json-schema/` is gitignored, so nothing moves there. The sibling card claimed in the same round (#19085) lands in `packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-registry.ts`; that file is not in this diff.

## Acceptance notes

- **To file (class a) — the `@example` block on `JobSchema` in `packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts` is refused verbatim.** It opens with `id: "job_sync_meta"`, and `job.id` was retired in 17.0.0 under ADR-0049 with a tombstone in this very file (`JOB_ID_RETIRED`). Probe, against the built package: `JobSchema.safeParse` of the example object answers `success: false` with `unrecognized_keys` naming `id` and the retirement prescription. The example is a source TSDoc only and does not reach `content/docs/references/**`, so the blast radius is an agent or a contributor reading the schema. Not fixed here: it is a different defect class from this card, so the bounded-in-place exemption does not open. Dedupe words: `job.id`, `job_sync_meta`, `JOB_ID_RETIRED`, `@example`, retired-key example.
- **Noted, not filed — the boundary type is a third door.** `JobSchedule.timezone` on `packages/spec/src/contracts/job-service.ts` is a plain optional `string` and is not judged by anything. The triage seat already ruled it outside this card and recorded that reading on the card's thread, which is its carrier; no open PR holding that file was measured from here. Nothing an author writes reaches it directly — it is the lowered runtime shape — so it is not one of the three filing classes.
- **Noted, not filed — `interval` and `once` carry no zone.** Confirmed, and pinned by a test in this PR so the claim stops being an assertion in a card.

## Verification

Every command below was run in this worktree; build and test runs went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. Exit codes were captured before any pipe.

| command | exit |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/system/job.test.ts` | 0 — 55 passed (55) |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` | 0 — 496 files, 14563 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | 0 — `tsc --noEmit`, `check:scripts-typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck` all clean |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | 0 after `gen:docs` — 16 artifacts, none stale |
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-undeclared-dep-imports.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-comment-mask-adoption.mjs` | 0 |
| self-tests: `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major` | 0 |

The dependency-closure leg is empty by construction: `packages/spec` declares only `zod` and `pg-connection-string`, so `@objectstack/spec^...` names no workspace package and there is nothing upstream to build. The spec `typecheck` script compiles the test layer too (`tsconfig.test.json`), so the new test file is inside what that green covers.

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derives 106 runnable commands for this five-path diff, plus 50 artifact-roster families, 11 wide-population families and 6 path-scheduled CI jobs that it states are outside that total. The repo-wide sweep is CI's run, not a local one; what is claimed above is the targeted set, and everything else is left to the required checks.
